author: Dongyu Zhao
version: 0.1
date: '2026-06-22'

## Directives

Text directives use one colon. The label parses inline Markdown. Attributes
use the generic directive attribute-list syntax inside braces. The AST exposes
an ordered string-to-string sequence without projecting it onto HTML.

Bare, unquoted, single-quoted, and double-quoted values all become strings.
The empty list is valid.

```````````````````````````````` example
Use :cite[Smith *et al.*]{id=smith class=paper data-kind=ref} here.
.
Document scope=1:1..1:67 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:67 anchor=null attributes={} children=3
    ├── Text scope=1:1..1:4 anchor=null attributes={} literal="Use " children=0
    ├── Directive scope=1:5..1:61 anchor="smith" attributes={.paper data-kind="ref"} name="cite" children=0
    │   └── DirectiveLabel scope=1:10..1:25 anchor=null attributes={} children=2
    │       ├── Text scope=1:11..1:16 anchor=null attributes={} literal="Smith " children=0
    │       └── Emphasis scope=1:17..1:24 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
    │           └── Text scope=1:18..1:23 anchor=null attributes={} literal="et al." children=0
    └── Text scope=1:62..1:67 anchor=null attributes={} literal=" here." children=0
````````````````````````````````

Inline attribute lists may span source lines. Their full source range belongs
to the directive, and subsequent inline nodes resume at the physical line and
column after the closing brace.

```````````````````````````````` example
:note[label]{title="one
two"} tail
.
Document scope=1:1..2:10 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..2:10 anchor=null attributes={} children=2
    ├── Directive scope=1:1..2:5 anchor=null attributes={title="one two"} name="note" children=0
    │   └── DirectiveLabel scope=1:6..1:12 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
    │       └── Text scope=1:7..1:11 anchor=null attributes={} literal="label" children=0
    └── Text scope=2:6..2:10 anchor=null attributes={} literal=" tail" children=0
````````````````````````````````

Numeric- and boolean-looking values remain strings in the AST/API
representation.

```````````````````````````````` example
:video{id=123 muted=true title="My Video"}
.
Document scope=1:1..1:42 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:42 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
    └── Directive scope=1:1..1:42 anchor="123" attributes={muted="true" title="My Video"} name="video" children=0
````````````````````````````````

An explicit empty attribute list is valid and is distinct from no attribute
list in the AST/API.

```````````````````````````````` example
:empty{}
.
Document scope=1:1..1:8 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:8 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
    └── Directive scope=1:1..1:8 anchor=null attributes={} name="empty" children=0
````````````````````````````````

Attribute values are strings. Bare attributes become empty strings, the last
duplicate key wins without moving its first slot, and quoted values may contain
spaces.

```````````````````````````````` example
:data[label]{muted dup=first dup=last unicode=中文😀 title="My Video"}
.
Document scope=1:1..1:74 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:74 anchor=null attributes={} children=2
    ├── Directive scope=1:1..1:12 anchor=null attributes={} name="data" children=0
    │   └── DirectiveLabel scope=1:6..1:12 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
    │       └── Text scope=1:7..1:11 anchor=null attributes={} literal="label" children=0
    └── Text scope=1:13..1:74 anchor=null attributes={} literal="{muted dup=first dup=last unicode=中文😀 title=\"My Video\"}" children=0
````````````````````````````````

`id` is an ordinary key: its last value wins while its first source position is
retained. Repeated `class` values accumulate, also in their first slot.

```````````````````````````````` example
:ordinary[label]{id=first class=red class=green class=blue id=last key=value}
.
Document scope=1:1..1:77 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:77 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
    └── Directive scope=1:1..1:77 anchor="last" attributes={.red .green .blue key="value"} name="ordinary" children=0
        └── DirectiveLabel scope=1:10..1:16 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
            └── Text scope=1:11..1:15 anchor=null attributes={} literal="label" children=0
````````````````````````````````

Malformed and unclosed attribute lists are not consumed as directive
attributes and remain ordinary Markdown text.

```````````````````````````````` example
:invalid{=value}
:open{title="value}
.
Document scope=1:1..2:19 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..2:19 anchor=null attributes={} children=4
    ├── Directive scope=1:1..1:8 anchor=null attributes={} name="invalid" children=0
    ├── Text scope=1:9..1:16 anchor=null attributes={} literal="{=value}" children=0
    ├── SoftBreak scope=1:17..1:17 anchor=null attributes={} children=0
    └── Directive scope=2:1..2:19 anchor=null attributes={title="\"value"} name="open" children=0
````````````````````````````````

The current directive implementation follows Remark's `#id` and `.class`
shortcut grammar. The shared target contract is Pandoc-shaped; Phase 2 replaces
this implementation behavior and updates these runtime fixtures atomically.

```````````````````````````````` example
:shortcut{#identifier}
:shortcut{.class}
.
Document scope=1:1..2:17 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..2:17 anchor=null attributes={} children=3
    ├── Directive scope=1:1..1:22 anchor="identifier" attributes={} name="shortcut" children=0
    ├── SoftBreak scope=1:23..1:23 anchor=null attributes={} children=0
    └── Directive scope=2:1..2:17 anchor=null attributes={.class} name="shortcut" children=0
````````````````````````````````

In the current implementation, adjacent `#` and `.` markers terminate the
current shorthand value and begin the next one without whitespace. Pandoc's
shared target grammar instead retains dots inside shorthand values; this case
pins the pre-migration runtime rather than the target contract.

```````````````````````````````` example
:id{#one.two}
:class{.one.two}
:colon{#one:two .three:four}
.
Document scope=1:1..3:28 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..3:28 anchor=null attributes={} children=5
    ├── Directive scope=1:1..1:13 anchor="one.two" attributes={} name="id" children=0
    ├── SoftBreak scope=1:14..1:14 anchor=null attributes={} children=0
    ├── Directive scope=2:1..2:16 anchor=null attributes={.one.two} name="class" children=0
    ├── SoftBreak scope=2:17..2:17 anchor=null attributes={} children=0
    └── Directive scope=3:1..3:28 anchor="one:two" attributes={.three:four} name="colon" children=0
````````````````````````````````

Text directive labels can contain links.

```````````````````````````````` example
:note[See [docs](https://example.com).]
.
Document scope=1:1..1:39 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:39 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
    └── Directive scope=1:1..1:39 anchor=null attributes={} name="note" children=0
        └── DirectiveLabel scope=1:6..1:39 anchor=null attributes={} children=3
            ├── Text scope=1:7..1:10 anchor=null attributes={} literal="See " children=0
            ├── Link scope=1:11..1:37 anchor=null attributes={} dest=url("https://example.com") title=null children=1
            │   └── Text scope=1:12..1:15 anchor=null attributes={} literal="docs" children=0
            └── Text scope=1:38..1:38 anchor=null attributes={} literal="." children=0
````````````````````````````````

Text directive labels can contain bracketed text that is not a link.

```````````````````````````````` example
:note[See [plain] text.]
.
Document scope=1:1..1:24 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:24 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
    └── Directive scope=1:1..1:24 anchor=null attributes={} name="note" children=0
        └── DirectiveLabel scope=1:6..1:24 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
            └── Text scope=1:7..1:23 anchor=null attributes={} literal="See [plain] text." children=0
````````````````````````````````

Text directives can appear inside link text.

```````````````````````````````` example
[Go :badge[beta]](/roadmap)
.
Document scope=1:1..1:27 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:27 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
    └── Link scope=1:1..1:27 anchor=null attributes={} dest=url("/roadmap") title=null children=2
        ├── Text scope=1:2..1:4 anchor=null attributes={} literal="Go " children=0
        └── Directive scope=1:5..1:16 anchor=null attributes={} name="badge" children=0
            └── DirectiveLabel scope=1:11..1:16 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
                └── Text scope=1:12..1:15 anchor=null attributes={} literal="beta" children=0
````````````````````````````````

Text directives can appear inside table cells.

```````````````````````````````` example table
| status |
| --- |
| :badge[beta] |
.
Document scope=1:1..3:16 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
└── Table scope=1:1..3:16 anchor=null attributes={} columns=[none:null] children=2
    ├── TableHead children=1
    │   └── TableRow scope=1:1..1:10 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
    │       └── TableCell scope=1:2..1:9 anchor=null attributes={} rowspan=1 colspan=1 children=1
    │           └── Text scope=1:3..1:8 anchor=null attributes={} literal="status" children=0
    ├── TableBody children=1
    │   └── TableRow scope=3:1..3:16 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
    │       └── TableCell scope=3:2..3:15 anchor=null attributes={} rowspan=1 colspan=1 children=1
    │           └── Directive scope=3:3..3:14 anchor=null attributes={} name="badge" children=0
    │               └── DirectiveLabel scope=3:9..3:14 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
    │                   └── Text scope=3:10..3:13 anchor=null attributes={} literal="beta" children=0
    └── TableFoot children=0
````````````````````````````````

A text directive with only a name is not recognized when it is followed by a
colon, so gemoji-compatible text remains text.

```````````````````````````````` example
:red:
.
Document scope=1:1..1:5 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:5 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
    └── Text scope=1:1..1:5 anchor=null attributes={} literal=":red:" children=0
````````````````````````````````

An empty label disambiguates a text directive before a following colon.

```````````````````````````````` example
:red[]:
.
Document scope=1:1..1:7 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:7 anchor=null attributes={} children=2
    ├── Directive scope=1:1..1:6 anchor=null attributes={} name="red" children=0
    │   └── DirectiveLabel scope=1:5..1:6 anchor=null attributes={} children=0
    └── Text scope=1:7..1:7 anchor=null attributes={} literal=":" children=0
````````````````````````````````

A LABEL IS SCANNED AT THE COLON, not paired with a closer found later. Both
branches continue, exactly as the attribute block's do: a label that closes is a
label, a label that does not is prose, and the directive stands either way.

```````````````````````````````` example
:a[b and :c[
.
Document scope=1:1..1:12 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:12 anchor=null attributes={} children=4
    ├── Directive scope=1:1..1:2 anchor=null attributes={} name="a" children=0
    ├── Text scope=1:3..1:9 anchor=null attributes={} literal="[b and " children=0
    ├── Directive scope=1:10..1:11 anchor=null attributes={} name="c" children=0
    └── Text scope=1:12..1:12 anchor=null attributes={} literal="[" children=0
````````````````````````````````

Because the whole construct is consumed there, nothing else is ever offered its
bytes. An emphasis run opened before the directive cannot pair with a marker
inside the label, and a code span inside one cannot protect the `]` that ends
it -- the label ended before either was looked for.

```````````````````````````````` example
*a :b[c*]
.
Document scope=1:1..1:9 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:9 anchor=null attributes={} children=2
    ├── Text scope=1:1..1:3 anchor=null attributes={} literal="*a " children=0
    └── Directive scope=1:4..1:9 anchor=null attributes={} name="b" children=0
        └── DirectiveLabel scope=1:6..1:9 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
            └── Text scope=1:7..1:8 anchor=null attributes={} literal="c*" children=0
````````````````````````````````

```````````````````````````````` example
:b[a`b]`c]
.
Document scope=1:1..1:10 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:10 anchor=null attributes={} children=2
    ├── Directive scope=1:1..1:7 anchor=null attributes={} name="b" children=0
    │   └── DirectiveLabel scope=1:3..1:7 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
    │       └── Text scope=1:4..1:6 anchor=null attributes={} literal="a`b" children=0
    └── Text scope=1:8..1:10 anchor=null attributes={} literal="`c]" children=0
````````````````````````````````

The scan is lexical: only a backslash escape and bracket balance decide where
the label ends, and nesting is capped at 32 as micromark caps it. Thirty-two
nested brackets are a label and thirty-three are prose.

```````````````````````````````` example
:a[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[x]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]
.
Document scope=1:1..1:69 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:69 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
    └── Directive scope=1:1..1:69 anchor=null attributes={} name="a" children=0
        └── DirectiveLabel scope=1:3..1:69 anchor=null attributes={} children=3
            ├── Text scope=1:4..1:33 anchor=null attributes={} literal="[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[" children=0
            ├── CrossLink scope=1:34..1:38 anchor=null attributes={} embedded=false dest=cross(path="x",anchor=null) label=null children=0
            └── Text scope=1:39..1:68 anchor=null attributes={} literal="]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]" children=0
````````````````````````````````

```````````````````````````````` example
:a[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[x]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]
.
Document scope=1:1..1:71 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:71 anchor=null attributes={} children=4
    ├── Directive scope=1:1..1:2 anchor=null attributes={} name="a" children=0
    ├── Text scope=1:3..1:34 anchor=null attributes={} literal="[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[" children=0
    ├── CrossLink scope=1:35..1:39 anchor=null attributes={} embedded=false dest=cross(path="x",anchor=null) label=null children=0
    └── Text scope=1:40..1:71 anchor=null attributes={} literal="]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]" children=0
````````````````````````````````

A directive name may contain a hyphen or underscore but may not begin or end
with one. This example previously expected `:-a[]` and `:_a[]` to be
directives; scripts/check-mdast-parity.mjs found the disagreement with
micromark-extension-directive, which rejects both. Its prose documents only the
trailing rule, so the leading one was confirmed against the implementation
directly: `:-a[]` and `:_a[]` produce no directive there, while `:1a[]` does.

```````````````````````````````` example
:a-[]
:-a[]
:_a[]
.
Document scope=1:1..3:5 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..3:5 anchor=null attributes={} children=5
    ├── Text scope=1:1..1:5 anchor=null attributes={} literal=":a-[]" children=0
    ├── SoftBreak scope=1:6..1:6 anchor=null attributes={} children=0
    ├── Text scope=2:1..2:5 anchor=null attributes={} literal=":-a[]" children=0
    ├── SoftBreak scope=2:6..2:6 anchor=null attributes={} children=0
    └── Text scope=3:1..3:5 anchor=null attributes={} literal=":_a[]" children=0
````````````````````````````````

A digit may begin a name, as it may in the reference implementation.

```````````````````````````````` example
:1a[]
.
Document scope=1:1..1:5 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:5 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
    └── Text scope=1:1..1:5 anchor=null attributes={} literal=":1a[]" children=0
````````````````````````````````

A name is CODE POINTS, like every other name in this grammar. `:café` is one
directive, not a directive called `caf` followed by the letter `é`, and the
block forms read the same names the inline form does.

```````````````````````````````` example
:café[x]
.
Document scope=1:1..1:9 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:9 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
    └── Directive scope=1:1..1:9 anchor=null attributes={} name="café" children=0
        └── DirectiveLabel scope=1:7..1:9 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
            └── Text scope=1:8..1:8 anchor=null attributes={} literal="x" children=0
````````````````````````````````

```````````````````````````````` example
::naïve{a=1}
.
Document scope=1:1..1:13 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
└── DirectiveBlock scope=1:1..1:13 anchor=null attributes={a="1"} name="naïve" children=0
````````````````````````````````

And punctuation ends a name whatever its width, which is the half a byte-wise
scan gets wrong in the other direction: an en dash is one code point of
punctuation and three bytes of none.

```````````````````````````````` example
a :b–c d
.
Document scope=1:1..1:10 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:10 anchor=null attributes={} children=3
    ├── Text scope=1:1..1:2 anchor=null attributes={} literal="a " children=0
    ├── Directive scope=1:3..1:4 anchor=null attributes={} name="b" children=0
    └── Text scope=1:5..1:10 anchor=null attributes={} literal="–c d" children=0
````````````````````````````````

An unquoted value may hold no quote of either kind, alongside the four it may
hold no `<`, `>`, `=` or backtick. Reaching one does not end the value, it
makes the block malformed.

```````````````````````````````` example
:n{a=b"c"}
.
Document scope=1:1..1:10 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:10 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
    └── Directive scope=1:1..1:10 anchor=null attributes={a="b\"c\""} name="n" children=0
````````````````````````````````

An underscore may not end a name either, the same as a hyphen.

```````````````````````````````` example
:a_[]
.
Document scope=1:1..1:5 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:5 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
    └── Text scope=1:1..1:5 anchor=null attributes={} literal=":a_[]" children=0
````````````````````````````````

Leaf directives use two colons on their own line. Repeated metadata keys use
their last value and are not projected onto HTML.

```````````````````````````````` example
::youtube[Video of a *cat*]{vid=01ab2cd3efg class=embed class=featured}
.
Document scope=1:1..1:71 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
└── DirectiveBlock scope=1:1..1:71 anchor=null attributes={.embed .featured vid="01ab2cd3efg"} name="youtube" children=0
    └── DirectiveLabel scope=1:10..1:27 anchor=null attributes={} children=2
        ├── Text scope=1:11..1:21 anchor=null attributes={} literal="Video of a " children=0
        └── Emphasis scope=1:22..1:26 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
            └── Text scope=1:23..1:25 anchor=null attributes={} literal="cat" children=0
````````````````````````````````

Container directives use three or more colons on their own line. A closing
fence must have at least the opening fence length.

```````````````````````````````` example
::::spoiler{id=outer class=red class=green class=blue}
He dies.

:::spoiler
She is born.
:::
::::
.
Document scope=1:1..7:4 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
└── DirectiveBlock scope=1:1..7:4 anchor="outer" attributes={.red .green .blue} name="spoiler" children=2
    ├── Paragraph scope=2:1..2:8 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
    │   └── Text scope=2:1..2:8 anchor=null attributes={} literal="He dies." children=0
    └── DirectiveBlock scope=4:1..6:3 anchor=null attributes={} name="spoiler" children=1
        └── Paragraph scope=5:1..5:12 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
            └── Text scope=5:1..5:12 anchor=null attributes={} literal="She is born." children=0
````````````````````````````````

If no closing fence is found, the container runs to the end of its parent.

```````````````````````````````` example
::::spoiler
These three are not enough to close
:::
So this line is also part of the container.
.
Document scope=1:1..4:43 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
└── DirectiveBlock scope=1:1..4:43 anchor=null attributes={} name="spoiler" children=1
    └── Paragraph scope=2:1..4:43 anchor=null attributes={} children=5
        ├── Text scope=2:1..2:35 anchor=null attributes={} literal="These three are not enough to close" children=0
        ├── SoftBreak scope=2:36..2:36 anchor=null attributes={} children=0
        ├── Text scope=3:1..3:3 anchor=null attributes={} literal=":::" children=0
        ├── SoftBreak scope=3:4..3:4 anchor=null attributes={} children=0
        └── Text scope=4:1..4:43 anchor=null attributes={} literal="So this line is also part of the container." children=0
````````````````````````````````

An indented colon run inside a container is content, not a closing fence.

```````````````````````````````` example
:::spoiler
    :::
:::
.
Document scope=1:1..3:3 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
└── DirectiveBlock scope=1:1..3:3 anchor=null attributes={} name="spoiler" children=1
    └── CodeBlock scope=2:5..2:7 anchor=null attributes={} info=null language=null literal=":::\n" fenced=false closed=true children=0
````````````````````````````````

The directive trigger characters are ordinary punctuation for emphasis
flanking: an underscore after `:` or `}` still opens emphasis exactly as
reference CommonMark requires.

```````````````````````````````` example
foo:_bar_
.
Document scope=1:1..1:9 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:9 anchor=null attributes={} children=2
    ├── Text scope=1:1..1:4 anchor=null attributes={} literal="foo:" children=0
    └── Emphasis scope=1:5..1:9 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
        └── Text scope=1:6..1:8 anchor=null attributes={} literal="bar" children=0
````````````````````````````````

```````````````````````````````` example
a}_b_
.
Document scope=1:1..1:5 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:5 anchor=null attributes={} children=2
    ├── Text scope=1:1..1:2 anchor=null attributes={} literal="a}" children=0
    └── Emphasis scope=1:3..1:5 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
        └── Text scope=1:4..1:4 anchor=null attributes={} literal="b" children=0
````````````````````````````````

`#name` and `.name` are shorthand for the `id` and `class` attributes. A
shorthand value ends at the next marker, so `{.a.b}` is two classes rather
than one class named `a.b`.

```````````````````````````````` example
:n{.a.b}
.
Document scope=1:1..1:8 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:8 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
    └── Directive scope=1:1..1:8 anchor=null attributes={.a.b} name="n" children=0
````````````````````````````````

`class` is the one attribute whose repeats accumulate, in source order, whether
they were written as shorthand or as `class=`. Every other name keeps the last
value.

```````````````````````````````` example
:n{class=x .y}
.
Document scope=1:1..1:14 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:14 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
    └── Directive scope=1:1..1:14 anchor=null attributes={.x .y} name="n" children=0
````````````````````````````````

`id` keeps the last value, like an ordinary name.

```````````````````````````````` example
:n{#a#b}
.
Document scope=1:1..1:8 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:8 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
    └── Directive scope=1:1..1:8 anchor="b" attributes={} name="n" children=0
````````````````````````````````

A shorthand marker with no name after it is not a valid attribute and
invalidates the block, which then takes the malformed-block fallback: the name
stands and the braces stay as text.

```````````````````````````````` example
:n{#}
.
Document scope=1:1..1:5 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:5 anchor=null attributes={} children=2
    ├── Directive scope=1:1..1:2 anchor=null attributes={} name="n" children=0
    └── Text scope=1:3..1:5 anchor=null attributes={} literal="{#}" children=0
````````````````````````````````

```````````````````````````````` example
:n{.}
.
Document scope=1:1..1:5 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:5 anchor=null attributes={} children=2
    ├── Directive scope=1:1..1:2 anchor=null attributes={} name="n" children=0
    └── Text scope=1:3..1:5 anchor=null attributes={} literal="{.}" children=0
````````````````````````````````

An ordinary attribute whose name is as long as `class` is not treated as one.

```````````````````````````````` example
:n{other=1 .a .b}
.
Document scope=1:1..1:17 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:17 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
    └── Directive scope=1:1..1:17 anchor=null attributes={.a .b other="1"} name="n" children=0
````````````````````````````````

The separator goes before every class value once something has accumulated, an
empty value included.

```````````````````````````````` example
:n{.a class="" .b}
.
Document scope=1:1..1:18 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:18 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
    └── Directive scope=1:1..1:18 anchor=null attributes={.a .b} name="n" children=0
````````````````````````````````

An empty value at the front accumulates nothing, so it contributes no leading
separator.

```````````````````````````````` example
:n{class="" .b}
.
Document scope=1:1..1:15 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:15 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
    └── Directive scope=1:1..1:15 anchor=null attributes={.b} name="n" children=0
````````````````````````````````

Shorthand also reaches the label-close probe, which validates the attribute
block after `]` before the label is accepted.

```````````````````````````````` example
:n[label]{#i .c}
.
Document scope=1:1..1:16 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:16 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
    └── Directive scope=1:1..1:16 anchor="i" attributes={.c} name="n" children=0
        └── DirectiveLabel scope=1:3..1:9 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
            └── Text scope=1:4..1:8 anchor=null attributes={} literal="label" children=0
````````````````````````````````

A text directive's colon may not sit next to another colon on either side. The
trailing rule keeps `:red:` available to emoji; the leading one keeps a run of
colons whole, so a run inside a paragraph is text rather than a shorter run
plus a directive. `::name` and `:::name` at the start of a line are leaf and
container directives and open through the block path instead.

```````````````````````````````` example
x ::a y
.
Document scope=1:1..1:7 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:7 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
    └── Text scope=1:1..1:7 anchor=null attributes={} literal="x ::a y" children=0
````````````````````````````````

A longer run behaves the same way; the directive never starts inside it.

```````````````````````````````` example
x ::::a y
.
Document scope=1:1..1:9 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:9 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
    └── Text scope=1:1..1:9 anchor=null attributes={} literal="x ::::a y" children=0
````````````````````````````````

A colon run with no space before it is text as well.

```````````````````````````````` example
x:::a
.
Document scope=1:1..1:5 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:5 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
    └── Text scope=1:1..1:5 anchor=null attributes={} literal="x:::a" children=0
````````````````````````````````

A quoted value must be separated from whatever follows it by whitespace or the
closing brace. Without that rule an unterminated quote lets the block run on
and swallow the rest of the paragraph.

```````````````````````````````` example
:n{a="x"b=1}
.
Document scope=1:1..1:12 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:12 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
    └── Directive scope=1:1..1:12 anchor=null attributes={a="x" b="1"} name="n" children=0
````````````````````````````````

An attribute name may not begin with punctuation, so a leading colon makes
the whole block invalid and it falls back to text. `:` and `.` are allowed
from the second character on, which is why `{a:b}` is a name.

```````````````````````````````` example
:x{:_a}
.
Document scope=1:1..1:7 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:7 anchor=null attributes={} children=2
    ├── Directive scope=1:1..1:2 anchor=null attributes={} name="x" children=0
    └── Text scope=1:3..1:7 anchor=null attributes={} literal="{:_a}" children=0
````````````````````````````````

A symbol is punctuation for this rule too.

```````````````````````````````` example
:x{a$b}
.
Document scope=1:1..1:7 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:7 anchor=null attributes={} children=2
    ├── Directive scope=1:1..1:2 anchor=null attributes={} name="x" children=0
    └── Text scope=1:3..1:7 anchor=null attributes={} literal="{a$b}" children=0
````````````````````````````````

Letters outside ASCII are names, not punctuation; the grammar is applied to
code points rather than bytes.

```````````````````````````````` example
:x{中文=1}
.
Document scope=1:1..1:12 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:12 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
    └── Directive scope=1:1..1:12 anchor=null attributes={中文="1"} name="x" children=0
````````````````````````````````

`:` and `.` inside a name are ordinary name characters.

```````````````````````````````` example
:x{a:b .c}
.
Document scope=1:1..1:10 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:10 anchor=null attributes={} children=4
    ├── Directive scope=1:1..1:2 anchor=null attributes={} name="x" children=0
    ├── Text scope=1:3..1:4 anchor=null attributes={} literal="{a" children=0
    ├── Directive scope=1:5..1:6 anchor=null attributes={} name="b" children=0
    └── Text scope=1:7..1:10 anchor=null attributes={} literal=" .c}" children=0
````````````````````````````````

A name may begin with a hyphen or an underscore, unlike a DIRECTIVE name, which
may not. Every other punctuation mark still ends the block.

```````````````````````````````` example
:n{-a=1 _b=2}
.
Document scope=1:1..1:13 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:13 anchor=null attributes={} children=2
    ├── Directive scope=1:1..1:2 anchor=null attributes={} name="n" children=0
    └── Text scope=1:3..1:13 anchor=null attributes={} literal="{-a=1 _b=2}" children=0
````````````````````````````````

A shorthand value is not a name. It ends at the next marker, at the block's end
or at whitespace, and six characters -- a quote of either kind, `<`, `=`, `>`
and a backtick -- reject it outright and take the block with them. Everything
else is a value character, so a class may contain an ampersand.

```````````````````````````````` example
:n{.a&b .c$d}
.
Document scope=1:1..1:13 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:13 anchor=null attributes={} children=2
    ├── Directive scope=1:1..1:2 anchor=null attributes={} name="n" children=0
    └── Text scope=1:3..1:13 anchor=null attributes={} literal="{.a&b .c$d}" children=0
````````````````````````````````

```````````````````````````````` example
:n{.a=b}
.
Document scope=1:1..1:8 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:8 anchor=null attributes={} children=2
    ├── Directive scope=1:1..1:2 anchor=null attributes={} name="n" children=0
    └── Text scope=1:3..1:8 anchor=null attributes={} literal="{.a=b}" children=0
````````````````````````````````

The two quotes are the same rule, but they never reach it: the raw scan of the
block tracks quoting, so `{.a"b}` has no closing brace outside a quote and is
malformed one step earlier. `=`, `<`, `>` and the backtick are the four that
this rule alone decides -- a pin on a quote proves nothing here, which a mutant
that deleted the whole reject set and survived is what said so.

```````````````````````````````` example
:n{.a`b}
.
Document scope=1:1..1:8 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:8 anchor=null attributes={} children=2
    ├── Directive scope=1:1..1:2 anchor=null attributes={} name="n" children=0
    └── Text scope=1:3..1:8 anchor=null attributes={} literal="{.a`b}" children=0
````````````````````````````````

Character references are decoded in an attribute's value, and in a shorthand's
value, and nowhere else in the attribute block: a name is taken as written
(Q20). An unknown reference is not a reference and stays as written.

```````````````````````````````` example
:n{a=&amp; b="&amp; &#65; &#x41;" .&amp; c=&notreal;}
.
Document scope=1:1..1:53 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:53 anchor=null attributes={} children=2
    ├── Directive scope=1:1..1:2 anchor=null attributes={} name="n" children=0
    └── Text scope=1:3..1:53 anchor=null attributes={} literal="{a=& b=\"& A A\" .& c=&notreal;}" children=0
````````````````````````````````

The decoding happens after the block has been scanned, never during it, so a
reference cannot produce a character that changes where the block ends or where
one attribute stops and the next begins.

```````````````````````````````` example
:n{a=x&#125;y b=p&#32;q}
.
Document scope=1:1..1:24 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:24 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
    └── Directive scope=1:1..1:24 anchor=null attributes={a="x&#125;y" b="p&#32;q"} name="n" children=0
````````````````````````````````

A reference in a NAME is not decoded, so `&` is what the name starts with, and
that is punctuation: the block is malformed and its source stays text -- where
the ordinary inline rules do decode it.

```````````````````````````````` example
:n{&#97;=v}
.
Document scope=1:1..1:11 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:11 anchor=null attributes={} children=2
    ├── Directive scope=1:1..1:2 anchor=null attributes={} name="n" children=0
    └── Text scope=1:3..1:11 anchor=null attributes={} literal="{a=v}" children=0
````````````````````````````````

The current engine requires the semicolon, as it does at inherited CommonMark
reference-decoding sites. The shared Pandoc target also retains semicolonless
references in unquoted values, so this measured Remark difference is deliberate
rather than implementation backlog.

```````````````````````````````` example
:n{a=&amp b=&#65}
.
Document scope=1:1..1:17 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:17 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
    └── Directive scope=1:1..1:17 anchor=null attributes={a="&amp" b="&#65"} name="n" children=0
````````````````````````````````

A leaf directive is a single line: the next line starts new content rather than
continuing it, unlike a container, which runs until its fence.

```````````````````````````````` example
::leaf[L]{a=b}
after
.
Document scope=1:1..2:5 anchor=null attributes={} children=2
├── DirectiveBlock scope=1:1..1:14 anchor=null attributes={a="b"} name="leaf" children=0
│   └── DirectiveLabel scope=1:7..1:9 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
│       └── Text scope=1:8..1:8 anchor=null attributes={} literal="L" children=0
└── Paragraph scope=2:1..2:5 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
    └── Text scope=2:1..2:5 anchor=null attributes={} literal="after" children=0
````````````````````````````````

An `=` promises a value. With none before the block ends, the whole attribute
block is malformed and its source stays text — an empty value would otherwise be
indistinguishable from the valueless `{a}`, which means something else.

```````````````````````````````` example
:x{a=}t
.
Document scope=1:1..1:7 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:7 anchor=null attributes={} children=2
    ├── Directive scope=1:1..1:6 anchor=null attributes={a=""} name="x" children=0
    └── Text scope=1:7..1:7 anchor=null attributes={} literal="t" children=0
````````````````````````````````

The same when only whitespace separates the `=` from the closer, and when the
block spans a line ending.

```````````````````````````````` example
:x{a= }t
.
Document scope=1:1..1:8 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:8 anchor=null attributes={} children=2
    ├── Directive scope=1:1..1:7 anchor=null attributes={a=""} name="x" children=0
    └── Text scope=1:8..1:8 anchor=null attributes={} literal="t" children=0
````````````````````````````````

```````````````````````````````` example
:x{a=
}t
.
Document scope=1:1..2:2 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..2:2 anchor=null attributes={} children=2
    ├── Directive scope=1:1..2:1 anchor=null attributes={a=""} name="x" children=0
    └── Text scope=2:2..2:2 anchor=null attributes={} literal="t" children=0
````````````````````````````````

An unquoted value may not contain `<`, `>`, `=`, or a backtick. Reaching one
does not end the value, it makes the block malformed.

```````````````````````````````` example
:x{a=b<c}t
.
Document scope=1:1..1:10 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:10 anchor=null attributes={} children=2
    ├── Directive scope=1:1..1:9 anchor=null attributes={a="b<c"} name="x" children=0
    └── Text scope=1:10..1:10 anchor=null attributes={} literal="t" children=0
````````````````````````````````

```````````````````````````````` example
:x{a=b>c}t
.
Document scope=1:1..1:10 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:10 anchor=null attributes={} children=2
    ├── Directive scope=1:1..1:9 anchor=null attributes={a="b>c"} name="x" children=0
    └── Text scope=1:10..1:10 anchor=null attributes={} literal="t" children=0
````````````````````````````````

```````````````````````````````` example
:x{a=b=c}t
.
Document scope=1:1..1:10 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:10 anchor=null attributes={} children=2
    ├── Directive scope=1:1..1:9 anchor=null attributes={a="b=c"} name="x" children=0
    └── Text scope=1:10..1:10 anchor=null attributes={} literal="t" children=0
````````````````````````````````

```````````````````````````````` example
:x{a=b`c}t
.
Document scope=1:1..1:10 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:10 anchor=null attributes={} children=2
    ├── Directive scope=1:1..1:9 anchor=null attributes={a="b`c"} name="x" children=0
    └── Text scope=1:10..1:10 anchor=null attributes={} literal="t" children=0
````````````````````````````````

A brace is not in that set: it is an ordinary character inside an unquoted
value, and a space ends the value and starts the next attribute's name.

```````````````````````````````` example
:x{a=b{c}t
.
Document scope=1:1..1:10 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:10 anchor=null attributes={} children=2
    ├── Directive scope=1:1..1:9 anchor=null attributes={a="b{c"} name="x" children=0
    └── Text scope=1:10..1:10 anchor=null attributes={} literal="t" children=0
````````````````````````````````

```````````````````````````````` example
:x{a=b c}t
.
Document scope=1:1..1:10 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:10 anchor=null attributes={} children=2
    ├── Directive scope=1:1..1:2 anchor=null attributes={} name="x" children=0
    └── Text scope=1:3..1:10 anchor=null attributes={} literal="{a=b c}t" children=0
````````````````````````````````

An unquoted value may span a line ending before it starts; the value itself is
what may not.

```````````````````````````````` example
:x{a=
b}t
.
Document scope=1:1..2:3 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..2:3 anchor=null attributes={} children=4
    ├── Directive scope=1:1..1:2 anchor=null attributes={} name="x" children=0
    ├── Text scope=1:3..1:5 anchor=null attributes={} literal="{a=" children=0
    ├── SoftBreak scope=1:6..1:6 anchor=null attributes={} children=0
    └── Text scope=2:1..2:3 anchor=null attributes={} literal="b}t" children=0
````````````````````````````````

D21's own pins, which the oracle has not got: a closing fence closes the
container and every block still open inside it. They are kept here, at the end,
because the oracle's ordering is otherwise adopted whole.

```````````````````````````````` example
a}*.foo.*
.
Document scope=1:1..1:9 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:9 anchor=null attributes={} children=2
    ├── Text scope=1:1..1:2 anchor=null attributes={} literal="a}" children=0
    └── Emphasis scope=1:3..1:9 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
        └── Text scope=1:4..1:8 anchor=null attributes={} literal=".foo." children=0
````````````````````````````````

A closing fence closes the container and every block still open inside it, and
the container ends on the fence's own line. Consuming the fence without closing
the block leaves the next non-blank line to arrive as a lazy paragraph
continuation: it is pulled inside the container and recorded on the fence's
line rather than its own.

```````````````````````````````` example
:::note
body
:::
after
.
Document scope=1:1..4:5 anchor=null attributes={} children=2
├── DirectiveBlock scope=1:1..3:3 anchor=null attributes={} name="note" children=1
│   └── Paragraph scope=2:1..2:4 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
│       └── Text scope=2:1..2:4 anchor=null attributes={} literal="body" children=0
└── Paragraph scope=4:1..4:5 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
    └── Text scope=4:1..4:5 anchor=null attributes={} literal="after" children=0
````````````````````````````````

The same, inside a block quote, where the misattribution moved content into the
quote as well.

```````````````````````````````` example
> :::note
> body
> :::
> after
.
Document scope=1:1..4:7 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
└── Callout scope=1:1..4:7 anchor=null attributes={} variant=null collapsed=null children=2
    ├── DirectiveBlock scope=1:3..3:5 anchor=null attributes={} name="note" children=1
    │   └── Paragraph scope=2:3..2:6 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
    │       └── Text scope=2:3..2:6 anchor=null attributes={} literal="body" children=0
    └── Paragraph scope=4:3..4:7 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
        └── Text scope=4:3..4:7 anchor=null attributes={} literal="after" children=0
````````````````````````````````

THE BLOCK FORM OF A DIRECTIVE HAS NO PARTIAL RECOVERY. The inline form keeps
the directive and gives up only the label or the attribute list; here one bad
attribute, or one byte of content after a good one, costs the whole line, and
what is left is a paragraph indistinguishable from prose. These examples pin
that AST behavior directly.

```````````````````````````````` example
::note{=value}

::note{a=b} trailing
.
Document scope=1:1..3:20 anchor=null attributes={} children=2
├── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:14 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
│   └── Text scope=1:1..1:14 anchor=null attributes={} literal="::note{=value}" children=0
└── Paragraph scope=3:1..3:20 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
    └── Text scope=3:1..3:20 anchor=null attributes={} literal="::note{a=b} trailing" children=0
````````````````````````````````

A DIRECTIVE NAME MAY CONTAIN UTF-8, AND AN UNCLOSED LABEL REMAINS PROSE.
The `é` is part of the directive name; the following bracket run is a separate
Text node because it never closes.

```````````````````````````````` example
:nnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnéz[unclosed
.
Document scope=1:1..1:52 anchor=null attributes={} children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:52 anchor=null attributes={} children=2
    ├── Directive scope=1:1..1:43 anchor=null attributes={} name="nnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnéz" children=0
    └── Text scope=1:44..1:52 anchor=null attributes={} literal="[unclosed" children=0
````````````````````````````````
